2_Introduction: The device shows the highest PCE of 15.194% with a VOC of 1.0363 V, a JSC of 21.882 mA/cm², and an FF of 67.0046%. The Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 perovskite film was prepared with a concentration of 1.73 mol/L. A two-tier spin-coating strategy (1000 rpm/10 s and 5000 rpm/40 s) produced a uniform and defect-minimized perovskite layer. During the second step, 200 µL of CB as anti-solvent was quickly dripped onto the centre of the perovskite film 8 s before the end of the spin-coating process. The wet film was annealed at 105 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite layer—engineered with a carefully balanced A-site cation mixture—exhibits enhanced phase stability and suppressed halide segregation due to the synergistic steric and electronic contributions of formamidinium (FA⁺) as the dominant cation, methylammonium (MA⁺) for lattice strain relaxation, and cesium (Cs⁺) for improved thermal tolerance and defect suppression at grain boundaries, while the near-ideal Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and reduced octahedral tilting minimize non-radiative recombination pathways; this compositional design, combined with the precisely controlled 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration, enables optimal nucleation density and intermediate phase evolution during crystallization, wherein the two-tier spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for initial wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent extraction) governs kinetic confinement of crystal growth, and the timed 200 µL chlorobenzene anti-solvent quench—applied 8 s before spin cessation—induces instantaneous supersaturation that favors homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening, thereby yielding a highly uniform, pinhole-free film with enlarged grains and reduced interfacial trap density; subsequent 105 °C/15 min thermal annealing completes ligand exchange, volatilizes residual solvents, and promotes Pb–I bond reorganization, collectively suppressing undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies while minimizing residual PbI₂ (as corroborated by XRD showing no detectable peak at ~12.6°) and eliminating parasitic 2D δ-phases (confirmed by absence of low-angle (001) reflections), resulting in a structurally coherent, low-strain perovskite lattice with narrow XRD peak FWHM indicative of high crystallinity and minimal microstrain; optical and PL mapping further reveal spatially homogeneous grayscale intensity and >3.5× enhancement in integrated PL intensity relative to control films, with monoexponential decay kinetics (τ₁ ≈ 385 ns) confirming drastic reduction in non-radiative recombination centers and uniform carrier lifetime across the film, directly linking morphological continuity and structural purity to efficient charge extraction; these interdependent crystallization, interface, and defect-control mechanisms—rooted in stoichiometric precision, kinetic engineering, and thermodynamic stabilization—ultimately yield VOC = 1.0363 V, JSC = 21.882 mA/cm², FF = 67.0046%, and PCE = 15.194%.
